prompt: A neatly hand-drawn geology lab worksheet titled 'Mineral Scratch-Test Grid': a single 4x4 table. The four ROW headers, top to bottom, are the minerals Fluorite, Quartz, Gypsum, Orthoclase, and the four COLUMN headers, left to right, are the SAME four minerals in the SAME order: Fluorite, Quartz, Gypsum, Orthoclase. In each cell you perform the scratch test: the ROW mineral is scraped against the COLUMN mineral. If the row mineral is HARDER than the column mineral it leaves a scratch, so draw a clear dark-red diagonal SCRATCH score line through that cell; if the row mineral is the same or SOFTER, it leaves no mark, so leave that cell clean (no red line). A mineral cannot scratch itself, so every cell on the main diagonal is left clean. Work out each of the sixteen cells from the real relative hardness of these four minerals and mark them correctly. Print ONLY the title and the mineral names in the headers -- do NOT print any hardness numbers, the words 'harder' or 'softer', any ranked list, or any answer key anywhere on the sheet. Clean cream worksheet paper, thin grey grid lines, black ink headers, red scratch lines.
easy_question: This picture was supposed to show a mineral scratch-test grid: a 4x4 table with mineral names as row and column headers, cells marked with a scratch line or left clean.
